comments.body:
RCA (rebar-debug Phase 1) — PROVEN root cause; genuine defect, already remediated on HEAD by 9ac2's guard.

CLASSIFICATION: real order-dependent test-state leak at the story's tree (5ce20c5350); NOT reproducible on current HEAD (b0add9ff4b) because commit 76ab5cebd2 (bug 9ac2, Gerrit 1282) landed the tree-wide fix AFTER this ticket was filed and after story 4e3e's two failing `make test` runs.

ROOT CAUSE: The victim assertion (tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py:149-159) uses caplog.at_level(logging.INFO) WITHOUT logger= — that raises only the ROOT logger's level. The asserted record (src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py:114, "llm call [%s]", INFO on rebar.llm.agent_call) is dropped earlier, at the ORIGINATING logger's effective-level walk, whenever the shared "rebar" logger holds a level > INFO. Every in-process CLI entrypoint call does exactly that: rebar._cli.main() -> install_stderr_handler("rebar") (src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:416-418) -> logger.setLevel(WARNING) when NOTSET (src/rebar/_logging.py:87-89; default WARNING from _resolve_level, REBAR_LOG_LEVEL unset). At the story's tree there was NO guard/restore, so the first such test poisoned the process for the rest of the run. Hundreds of in-process CLI tests collect before tests/unit (e.g. tests/interfaces/contracts/test_workflow_cli_output_contract.py — present in the story tree, calls rebar._cli.main in-process), hence: deterministic full-suite failure, pass in isolation and in module runs (no CLI test precedes there). Single-victim blast radius: census shows test_agent_call_seam.py:149 is the suite's only real no-logger caplog.at_level(INFO) whose asserted record originates under "rebar".

DISCRIMINATING EVIDENCE (worktree epic-2f4c, HEAD b0add9ff4b):
- E1: full unit-tree collection, run victim only -> PASSED (no import/collection-time poisoning).
- E2: full `make test` order (9799 tests) with a probe plugin diffing manager.disable / root level / {rebar, rebar.llm, rebar.llm.agent_call} level/disabled/propagate/filters/handlers after every test -> victim PASSED at position 4702, ZERO poisoning events; only benign rebar.nhandlers 1->2 (stderr handler install; level restored per-test by the 9ac2 guard); manager.disable stayed 0 throughout.
- E3: all 458 post-victim modules THEN the victim, same probe -> 5072 passed, victim green, zero poisoning. E2+E3: no live contaminator anywhere on HEAD (only the known macOS env failures: safe.bareRepository / ref_lock / sync_remote).
- E4a (mechanism, RED): scratch pair, NO guard — test A runs rebar._cli.main(["--help"]) in-process (real entrypoint; asserts rebar level == WARNING after), test B is the victim test byte-for-byte -> B FAILS with StopIteration at the same line. Exact story signature reproduced on demand.
- E4b (fix confirmation, GREEN): identical pair + faithful replica of the 9ac2 guard (tests/conftest.py:489-508 wiring tests/_log_integrity.py) -> 2 passed. The guard's per-test level restore is necessary and sufficient.
- E4c (rival killed): identical pair but contaminator applies the exact b718 postcondition instead (rebar setLevel(INFO) + propagate=False, story-tree review_bot/config.py:146) -> 2 passed. pytest 9.1.1's catching_logs attaches its capture handler directly to non-propagating loggers and INFO does not filter the record, so b718 CANNOT explain this victim. The WARNING level-pin is the only vector matching the signature.
- Static rivals killed: pytest 9.1.1 _force_enable_logging self-heals logging.disable inside at_level; setLevel invalidates the manager cache (no stale isEnabledFor cache).
- Corroboration: 76ab5cebd2's commit message names this exact test as "the live cause of the order-dependent StopIteration"; victim test, agent_call.py, _logging.py are byte-identical between 5ce20c5350 and HEAD — only the guard differs.

MECHANISM (one line): unguarded process-global logger state — install_stderr_handler's WARNING pin on the shared "rebar" logger persisted across tests; caplog.at_level(INFO) without logger= cannot rescue it because the drop happens at the originating logger, not root.

SIBLING-BUG CANDIDATES (named, not filed): (1) tests/_log_integrity.py guards ONLY the "rebar" root logger — levels/disabled/filters on intermediates (rebar.llm, rebar.llm.agent_call) and the "rebar_reconciler" root are unguarded; a future setLevel there reproduces this class. (2) tests/unit/test_review_bot.py's _clear_reviewbot_log_handlers resets the rebar level to NOTSET rather than the snapshotted baseline — masked by the guard today, latent divergence. (3) The victim's own no-logger at_level(INFO) stays fragile-by-design; any unguarded level vector re-bites it first.

PHASE-2 SKETCH + RED ORACLE: root-cause fix (9ac2 guard + b718 removal) is already on main and E2/E3 prove no live leak, so remaining work here is the regression oracle + hardening, not a new fix. Suggested RED oracle (deterministic 2-node order, no full suite): pytester case running [in-process rebar._cli.main test] then [the telemetry test] with the log-integrity guard disabled -> expect the StopIteration failure; same pair WITH the guard -> green (exactly E4a/E4b). tests/unit/test_caplog_coverage_integrity.py's _LEVEL_POISONED_TESTS pytester pair already encodes the generic version — extend it (or add one case) using the real entrypoint (rebar._cli.main) + the real victim assertion so the historical failure is pinned verbatim. Optional hardening: pass logger="rebar.llm.agent_call" (or "rebar") to at_level in the victim test; consider widening the guard to snapshot the "rebar*" subtree. Closing as fixed-by-9ac2 with the oracle addition is a defensible minimal Phase 2.

compiled_state.description:
## Context
Two clean `make test` runs while implementing story 4e3e-d36f-53b9-4c1e each completed 8,906 tests successfully and failed only `tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py::test_success_telemetry_survives_an_empty_usage_dict`: `caplog.records` contained no `llm call [` INFO record. The node passes in isolation, its full module passes 12/12, and the immediately preceding module plus it pass 21/21. This demonstrates a broader full-suite order/global-logging-state leak unrelated to bridge-fsck.

## Approach
- Reproduce with a minimized ordered prefix of the full collection and identify the earlier test or fixture that mutates logger level, propagation, handlers, disable state, or capture integration without restoring it.
- Fix the leaking test/fixture or make the telemetry contract robust at the correct boundary; do not weaken the assertion merely to hide global state.
- Add a regression that fails when the contaminating test and telemetry test run in the proven order.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A minimized deterministic test order reproduces the missing INFO capture before the fix and passes after it.
- [ ] The responsible logger/capture global state is restored between tests, with a regression proving isolation.
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py` passes alone, after the contaminating test, and in the complete non-integration suite.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `make test` pass.

## Evidence
Both full-suite failures and focused pass counts are recorded on discovered-from story 4e3e-d36f-53b9-4c1e.
